Let <MATH_0001>
be two <MATH_0002>-morphisms. Then <MATH_0003>
is an automorphism of <MATH_0004> over <MATH_0005>.
Hence if <MATH_0006>
is proper, then by the valuative criterion of properness
(Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0001>)
we can find <MATH_0007> whose restriction to
<MATH_0008> is <MATH_0009>.
Then we can use <MATH_0010> to define an equivalence
between the category of dotted arrows for <MATH_0011>
to the category of dotted arrows for <MATH_0012> by
sending <MATH_0013> to <MATH_0014>.
The final statement is clear.

Assume given a <MATH_0001>-commutative diagram
<MATH_0002>
with the right square <MATH_0003>-cartesian. Choose a <MATH_0004>-arrow
<MATH_0005>. Set
<MATH_0006>, <MATH_0007> and let
<MATH_0008> be the composition of
<MATH_0009> with the <MATH_0010>-arrow implicit in the <MATH_0011>-commutativity
of the right square. Then the category of dotted arrows
for the left square and <MATH_0012> is equivalent to the category of dotted
arrows for the outer rectangle and <MATH_0013>.

(We do not know how to prove the analogue of this lemma if instead
of the category of dotted arrows we look at the set of isomorphism
classes of morphisms producing two <MATH_0001>-commutative
triangles as in Lemma <REF_0001>;
in fact this analogue may very well be wrong.)
First proof: this lemma is a special case of Categories, 
Lemma <REF_0002>.
Second proof: we are allowed to replace
<MATH_0002> by the <MATH_0003>-fibre product
<MATH_0004>
as described in Categories, Lemma
<REF_0003>.
Then the object <MATH_0005> becomes the triple <MATH_0006>.
Then we can go from a dotted arrow <MATH_0007> for the
outer rectangle to a dotted arrow <MATH_0008>
for the left square by taking <MATH_0009> and
<MATH_0010> and
<MATH_0011>. Details omitted.
